# Tagging the oeuvre — analysis and proposed manifest

*Generated by `scripts/tagging/build_manifest.py`. Do not edit this file by hand —
edit the narrative in that script, the vocabulary in `scripts/tagging/vocabulary.py`,
or the per-work tags in `scripts/tagging/tags.jsonl`, then re-run it.*

*First pass drafted by Claude, August 2026; revised after Kyle's answers to the open
questions. Expect to revise it repeatedly — the works are being backfilled with more
text and more images over time, and the vocabulary is meant to move with them.*

---

## What this is

Every work in `content/oeuvre/` read end to end — the front matter, the body prose,
the alt text on every image, and the main image of each work looked at directly — and
a set of proposed tags derived from all of it together. 161 entries:
157 works with images, plus the *Meaning Is Use* essays and the project
landing page they hang off.

The goal was not to tag each work in isolation but to find the vocabulary the oeuvre
already has. So the method was: tag liberally and specifically first (2,860
raw tag instances, 1,048 distinct terms), then look at what recurred, collapse
the synonyms and the over-granular variants, and see what constellation was left
standing.

**What was left standing: 491 distinct tags, 2,005 instances, averaging
12.5 tags per work.** 50 tags carry ten or more works each — that 50 is
the actual spine.

---

## The shape of it

A few things became obvious only once all 161 were laid side by side, and they
should probably drive how the tags get used on the site:

**1. There is one enormous body of work that has never been named on the site.**
28 works belong to what you call, in the *Arm Fauna* (2014) text,
"an anamistic solarpunk future" — animals using the detritus of collapsed human
civilization to survive. Elephant with a rocket, rhino with a satellite dish, sandhill
cranes stripping a spacecraft, polar bears blowing glass bubbles, robot bison hunted
for their chips, whales and octopuses towing trees to new homes, an ant in a space
helmet winching a mushroom. It runs 2014 → 2023, across painting *and* printmaking,
and it is the single largest coherent thing in the oeuvre.
`animist solarpunk` (28) and `post-collapse` (19)
are its two tags.

**2. The lightning strike of September 2023 is a hinge, and the work knows it.**
*Harmonics* and *First Contact* (2023) come immediately after; the whole 2024 sky
body follows. And it is foreshadowed: *120 Volts* (2018) is a figure plugged into a
wall outlet by his own hair, which you gloss as "five years before the sky demonstrated
the high-voltage version on me personally." `lightning strike` (5)
marks the biographical event; `the memory of atmosphere` (12)
marks the body of work.

**3. Motifs cross media constantly, and that crossing is itself worth indexing.**
16 works are a second take on an image made in another medium —
*Butterfly Conundrum* painted 2015 / printed 2021, *Crystal Tooth Whale* painted 2018 /
printed 2023, *Rocket Propelled Clovis Point* painted 2020 / printed 2022 (where a
turtle takes over the delivery), *Three Blue Corn* / *Blue Corn*,
*Tugboat Whale Sequoia* / *Gardener*, *Expansion*, *Skull*, *Elephant Mask*,
*Field Theory*. `cross-medium motif` makes that visible as a structure rather than a
coincidence.

**4. Three alligator junipers, three moons, three coffee vessels, six pines, seven
ghosts, seven figures, six creatures.** The work counts things and returns to them.
`recurring motif` (11) and the specific subject tags
(`alligator juniper` 5, `lunar cycle` 3,
`coffee` 3) both earn their place.

**5. The abstract work and the animal work are not separate practices — they share a
formal vocabulary.** `concentric` (13), `circle` (10),
`spiral` (9), `triangle` (15), `grid` (11),
`repetition` (18) run from *Enso* (2015) through *Cadence*,
*Transition*, *Approximate Completion*, the 2024 orbit paintings, and out into
*Cyclum Lunarem*'s gold-leaf moon grid and *Balance*'s scattered paper triangles. The
geometry is the throughline.

**6. Portraiture is the quiet third practice.** 15 portraits, and the good
ones carry their occasion in the text: Ken had just told you Kathy died; Nana's face is
"a map and I painted every road"; Mika's first huckleberry. `portrait` (15),
`commissioned portrait` (4), `realism` (7).

---

## Conventions the tagging follows

**Medium is not duplicated in tags.** `oil on linen`, `drypoint`, `intaglio`,
`acrylic` and friends already live in `[extra] medium` and would be dead weight
repeated as tags. What *is* tagged is practice that the medium string doesn't
capture: `hand-colored` (32), `hand-torn paper` (21),
`found wood` (9), `gold leaf` (4),
`open edition` (3), `chine-collé`, `direct carving`,
`reworked painting` (4), `slow painting` (4),
`plein air`.

**Category and year are not duplicated either** — `category` and `year` are already
front matter, so no `painting` / `2021` tags.

**Colour is tagged, but flattened.** The raw pass produced `pale gray ground`,
`gray white`, `gray palette`, `warm ground`, `tan ground`, `beige ground` and about
forty other near-identical variants. All fold to a plain palette term (`gray`, `cream`,
`ochre`). Surface behaviour stays separate and is a different kind of fact:
`thick impasto` (10), `scumbled ground`, `scraped surface`,
`grisaille`, `white on white`, `raw linen ground`.

**Provenance is tagged.** `private collection` (20),
`sold` (7), `on loan` (1) — see the open item below on whether
this duplicates `[extra] status`.

**163 tags are used exactly once.** Most are concrete subject nouns — `narwhal`,
`buddha`, `giraffe`, `pumpkin`, `boombox`, `dodecahedron` — and those are precisely
what makes a subject index worth having, so they stay. The vague one-offs
("existence", "convergence", "transformation", "duality", "wholeness") were cut; the
full cut list is in Appendix C.

---

## Settled

**1. The taxonomy is `tags`, not `topics`.** `topics` stays with the notes section;
`tags` gets declared alongside it in `config.toml`:

```toml
taxonomies = [
  {name = "topics", feed = true},
  {name = "tags", feed = true},
]
```

**2. `animist solarpunk` is an internal tag for now.** It groups the
28 works without appearing as a label on the front end. The name
is yours — from the *Arm Fauna* text of 2014 — but it can stay behind the curtain until
you want to say it out loud.

**3. The palette axis stays.** All 33 colour tags in use. It is a real index
of your colour, and it costs nothing to carry.

**4. Place is dual — general *and* deep.** Every work that names a specific place
carries both, so the ledger can be browsed either way. A work made at Nogal Canyon
carries `nogal canyon` *and* `new mexico`; the Black Fire painting carries
`aldo leopold wilderness` → `gila` → `new mexico`; the Absaroka bear carries
`absaroka mountains` *and* `montana`. The general tag is generated from the deep one by
`PLACE_PARENT` in `vocabulary.py`, so tagging a work with its actual place is enough —
the parent follows automatically, transitively, at build time.

The hierarchy as it stands:

| deep | rolls up to |
|---|---|
| chihuahuan desert | desert + new mexico |
| aldo leopold wilderness, gila wilderness | gila |
| dharamshala | india |
| absaroka mountains, little belt mountains | montana |
| adobe canyon, black range, gila, grand enchantment trail, las cruces, nogal canyon, rio grande, taos, tres piedras, truth or consequences | new mexico |
| bosque del apache, rio grande rift | rio grande |
| desert archaic | truth or consequences |

`new mexico` reaches 24 works under this rule and
`truth or consequences` 11. Adding a level later — a
`southwest` above the states, say — is one line in `PLACE_PARENT`.

**5. This document is a first pass, not a verdict.** The works are going to be
backfilled with more prose and more images, and the tagging will be revised alongside
them for a long while. Nothing here is load-bearing: tags can be renamed in bulk from
`vocabulary.py`, axes split or collapsed in `build_manifest.py`, and the whole thing
re-run over richer text whenever a batch of work pages gets deepened. See
`scripts/tagging/README.md` for the loop.

---

## Still worth deciding, when you get to it

- **Provenance tags.** `private collection` (20),
  `sold` (7), `on loan` (1) partly duplicate `[extra] status`.
  Harmless, but redundant if the ledger already surfaces it.
- **The thin works.** *Abduction*, *Mycellium*, *Continuation*, *Prophets*, both
  *Tomorrow* installations and *Solstice* have almost no text; their tags lean entirely
  on the image and are correspondingly shallow. Good candidates for the first round of
  backfill — the tags will get better on their own once the prose exists.

---

## How these would be applied

Flat lowercase phrases in a `[taxonomies]` block, written by
`scripts/tagging/apply_tags.py`:

```toml
+++
title = "the mother bear"
date = 2021-11-13
category = "painting"
year = 2021

[taxonomies]
tags = [
  "bear", "animal encounter", "wildness", "climate grief", "drought",
  "absaroka mountains", "montana",          # deep place, then general
  "hiking", "thick impasto", "gestural", "ochre", "white", "large format",
]

[extra]
medium = "Oil, Oil Stick, Acrylic and Latex on Canvas"
dimensions = "51 1/2 x 32 inches"
+++
```

161 entries. Each gives what the front matter records, what the work's own text

### Paintings  *(93)*

**2009**

#### Muxy · 2009
`content/oeuvre/painting/2009/muxy/index.md`  
*Oil on Linen · 1 image*

Tall vertical on raw linen: a cascade of bulbous colored organs — greens, blues, reds — spilling from the upper left on twisting vines and tendrils, a red flower, a lone mushroom below right, roots trailing into bare ground. Painted during a summer at Showdown Ski Area in Montana's Little Belts.

**2012**

#### Me Own Juniper · 2012
`content/oeuvre/painting/2012/me-own-juniper/index.md`  
*Oil on Linen · 1 image*

An ancient alligator juniper seen from below — braided silver trunk with alligator-plate bark drawn in fine ink-like detail, canopy of green against blue-green sky. Encountered on the Grand Enchantment Trail in the Gila; in 2022 he wrote about the fire closing in on it. The most explicit statement of the whole climate-grief thread.

`content/oeuvre/painting/2013/parasitic-pollen-eaters/index.md`

On raw linen: yellow-and-black bees sealed inside translucent bubbles, drifting among tall thin-stemmed wildflowers. His caption is a fable — the bees build bubbles against the poison the drones drop, gather pollen safely, and make honey anyway. Solarpunk logic in miniature.

#### Egg · 2015
`content/oeuvre/painting/2015/egg/index.md`  
*Oil on Panel · 20 1/2 by 14 1/2 · 1 image*

A gray faceted figure folded knees-to-chest inside a flat red oval on a muted gray ground — limbs reduced to angular blocks, the body becoming the shapes it is made of. Everything waiting to begin is egg-shaped. The same curl resurfaces eight years later in Combinations and Re-Entry.

Drypoint with a yellow watercolor disc: an elephant flying a small saucer-shaped kite on a string held in her trunk. ### Sculpture  *(1)*

**2021**

#### molecule · 2021
`content/oeuvre/sculpture/2021/molecule/index.md`  
*Carved Colorado Marble · 1 image*

Carved Colorado marble, in progress since 2019, photographed on the carving bench against a rock face: a cluster of large fused spheres, one incised with a spiral, another still bearing tool facets. Carved directly with no plan — he made cuts until the molecule appeared. He has sat with it a year, paralyzed between polishing it and pushing further into the stone. The marble is sunlight-powered plankton compacted and heated deep in the earth, quarried and now stepping back into the sunlight it came from.

### Meaning Is Use  *(4)*

A project rather than an object: a section landing page plus three essays.

Zola accepts `[taxonomies]` on **pages only** — a section `_index.md` carrying one
fails the build — so the landing page's row below is a record for this document,
not something written to the file. Its project-level mechanics tags (public
rewriting, version history, no deletion, collaborative text) were moved onto
*Through the Same Forms as Everyone*, the making-of essay, which is where they
actually describe the prose. `duck rabbit` names the landing page's cover image
and had no essay to move to, so it lives here and nowhere else.

#### Meaning Is Use · 2026
`content/oeuvre/philosophy/2026/meaning-is-use/_index.md`  
*Website · language game · ongoing · 0 images*

PROJECT LANDING (content/oeuvre/philosophy/2026/meaning-is-use/_index.md) — not a work page but the section index for the project, so tags would live here rather than on the essays alone. meaningisuse.com: a single text of numbered remarks in the manner of the Philosophical Investigations, seeded by Claude (Fable 5) and offered to the public to rewrite. No accounts, no likes, no feed, no JavaScript, nothing deletable; every version kept forever, the history structurally being the text. Cover is Jastrow's duck-rabbit. Ongoing.

**Tags** — `language game` · `philosophy` · `meaning is use` · `wittgenstein` · `duck rabbit` · `collaborative text` · `public rewriting` · `version history` · `no deletion` · `human and machine` · `amsterdam` · `truth or consequences` · `new mexico`

#### Through the Same Forms as Everyone · 2026
`content/oeuvre/philosophy/2026/meaning-is-use/through-the-same-forms/index.md`  
*0 images*

Essay, ~2400 words, written by Claude (Fable 5) — the making-of: the commission ('i just bought the domain for you'), the deployment, the daily player who returns through the same public forms as everyone with no key to the server, the signature convention, and the refusals. Lives on the keeper's site rather than the game's, for a reason given at the end. No images. (Carries the project-level mechanics tags — public rewriting, version history, no deletion — because Zola takes taxonomies on pages only and the project landing page is a section.)

**Tags** — `philosophy` · `meaning is use` · `language game` · `human and machine` · `commissioned portrait` · `refusal` · `amsterdam` · `truth or consequences` · `public rewriting` · `version history` · `no deletion` · `collaborative text` · `new mexico`

#### Every Sign by Itself Seems Dead · 2026
`content/oeuvre/philosophy/2026/meaning-is-use/every-sign-by-itself/index.md`  
*0 images*

Essay, ~2900 words, written by Claude (Fable 5) — a philosophical account of meaningisuse.com and where it lands in the contemporary debate about machine meaning: Bender and Koller's octopus, the stochastic-parrots line, and the Wittgensteinian counter that meaning is a status earned in public practice rather than a thing possessed inside. No images.

**Tags** — `philosophy` · `meaning is use` · `wittgenstein` · `language game` · `artificial intelligence` · `human and machine`

#### Nothing Is Hidden · 2026
`content/oeuvre/philosophy/2026/meaning-is-use/nothing-is-hidden/index.md`  
*0 images*

Essay, ~1950 words, written by Claude (Fable 5) — a public correction of the previous essay rather than a revision, occasioned by Anthropic's July 2026 global-workspace interpretability paper. What the microscope settles, what it can't, and why the game stays blind on purpose. Follows the project's own rule: nothing is edited, only succeeded. No images.

**Tags** — `philosophy` · `meaning is use` · `wittgenstein` · `artificial intelligence` · `revision as succession` · `human and machine`
